key_insight: Coordinating multimodal AIGC tools with a hierarchical agentic framework yields globally coherent, style-consistent webpages by planning at the page level and delegating element-level generation to specialized agents.
problem_solved: Addresses style inconsistency and poor global coherence when integrating isolated AIGC modules for images, video, and UI components into automated webpage generation.
method: Top-level planner agent produces a global page plan and style guide (layout, color, typography, content roles).
Specialized multimodal sub-agents generate element-level assets (images, components, micro-interactions) guided by the global plan and iterative feedback.
Hierarchical coordination loop enforces consistency via cross-agent verification and refinement until layout-level coherence is achieved.
impact: Enables scalable, automated webpage design that preserves visual identity and UX coherence, reducing manual tuning and making multimodal AIGC practical for production UI workflows.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing hierarchical agents: planner → sub-agents → verifier
Before/after webpage examples highlighting improved style consistency
Pipeline flowchart: planning → generation → verification → refinement
Style-guide overlay (colors, typography, spacing) mapped onto a generated page
paper_title: MM-WebAgent: A Hierarchical Multimodal Web Agent for Webpage Generation
paper_authors: Yan Li, Zezi Zeng, Yifan Yang, Yuqing Yang, Ning Liao
